audit_findings.title: Silvus share-settled earnout is missing from the common-share claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $127 million filed fair value, or $0.75 per valuation share; $600 million contractual maximum, or $3.52 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The earnout must enter either as additional performance-conditioned shares in the denominator or as a liability deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In connection with the acquisition of Silvus, the Seller will have the potential to earn contingent earnout consideration upon the achievement of certain financial targets payable in shares of common stock of up to $ 600 million in total, comprised of up to $ 150 million for the annual period from July 5, 2026 through July 3, 2027 and up to $ 450 million for the annual period from July 4, 2027 through July 1, 2028 (with the potential to earn catch-up earnout consideration based on performance in the annual period from July 4, 2027 through July 1, 2028 if the maximum earnout for the annual period from July 5, 2026 through July 3, 2027 is not earned).
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated: the latest filing records a $127 million earnout liability, while the valuation neither deducts it nor includes settlement shares. At current fair value, correcting it would reduce base value from $216.25 to about $215.50 per share. Even deducting the full $600 million maximum would reduce base value only to about $212.73, a 1.63% change, and bull value to about $237.02, still $235.71 below the $472.73 market price. The claim therefore does not change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the purchase agreement's settlement-price formula and performance thresholds, then replace the liability with scenario-conditioned shares or deduct scenario-weighted earnout value in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may require acquisition spending that owner earnings does not deduct
audit_findings.magnitude: $4,916 million of 2025 acquisitions and investments, equal to 240.4% of $2,044.6 million anchor OE; $463 million, or 83.4%, of the $555 million H1 2026 revenue increase was acquisition-related
audit_findings.mechanism: The model compounds OE at 7% and 9% without charging the acquisition purchase prices, incremental financing, integration costs, or other capital required to obtain acquired growth.
audit_findings.evidence: In order to position ourselves to take advantage of growth opportunities or to meet other strategic needs such as product or technology gaps, we have made, and expect to continue to make, strategic acquisitions that involve significant risks and uncertainties.
audit_findings.explanation: It is not yet demonstrated that the forecast rates require acquisitions, but the possibility is materially supported by the filed record: 2025 acquisition and investment spending exceeded two years of anchor OE, and acquisitions supplied most of the reported H1 2026 revenue increase. Announced but unclosed transactions of $1.5 billion and C$675 million reinforce that acquisitions remain part of the growth program. Treating acquisition-supported growth as costless can materially overstate sustainable OE and its capitalized value.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct historical organic versus acquired revenue, operating earnings, and OE; then rerun each scenario using either an organically supportable growth rate or recurring acquisition outlays, integration costs, and associated interest matched to the acquired growth.

audit_findings.title: Hytera litigation recoveries may be capitalized as recurring owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $157 million 2025 gain, equal to 7.7% of anchor OE; $61 million 2024 gain; $141 million 2025 cash received net of withholding taxes
audit_findings.mechanism: If not purged, the nonrecurring recovery increases the OE anchor and historical trend and is then multiplied through the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: During the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, the Company recognized gains on the Hytera litigation of $ 157 million and $ 61 million, respectively, for amounts recovered through legal proceedings due to theft of the Company's trade secrets.
audit_findings.explanation: The gains and their nonrecurring character are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not reconcile the $2,044.6 million OE anchor closely enough to establish whether they remain in OE. If the 2025 gain is retained, the exposure is potentially meaningful because it equals 7.7% of the anchor; however, it is not a demonstrated valuation error until the OE reconciliation confirms omission of the purge.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2024 and 2025 reported earnings line by line to OE, identify the tax treatment of each Hytera gain, remove the full after-tax recovery if retained, and rerun both the trend calculation and all scenarios; apply the same treatment to the $60 million H1 2026 gain in any updated anchor.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded pension claims and noncash pension income may be omitted
audit_findings.magnitude: $124 million 2025 net periodic benefit, equal to 6.1% of anchor OE; latest filed noncurrent defined-benefit liabilities less related assets were $352 million, or $2.07 per valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: Noncash pension income can inflate OE, while an unfunded benefit obligation not captured through forecast cash contributions is a claim that should reduce the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We have underfunded pension obligations, in part resulting from the fact that we retained almost all of the U.S. pension liabilities and a major portion of our non-U.S. pension liabilities following our past divestitures.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest balance sheet demonstrates a net noncurrent defined-benefit claim, but the OE workpaper is absent, so the record cannot establish whether pension income was already removed or whether cash contributions were captured. The $124 million benefit is large enough to require reconciliation, while the identifiable latest net balance-sheet claim alone is about 1.0% of base equity value. Materiality of the combined correction remains unresolved because normalization and double-counting cannot be determined from the supplied valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile OE to remove the $124 million 2025 net periodic benefit if present, substitute sustainable company cash funding, reconcile all funded and overfunded plans at July 4, 2026, and deduct only the net deficit not already reflected through forecast contributions.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor is not a full-year post-Silvus run rate
audit_findings.mechanism: The mixed-period FY2025 OE anchor contains only about five months of Silvus, while the bridge uses July 2026 balances; omitted post-acquisition earnings can understate OE, whereas full-year interest, working capital, compensation, and integration requirements can overstate it.
audit_findings.evidence: On August 6, 2025, the Company acquired Silvus from Silvus Technologies Group LLC (the "Seller").
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated and is reasonably capable of materially changing the anchor. H1 2026 filings show $463 million of acquisition-related revenue contribution, a $102 million year-over-year increase in net interest expense, a $109 million increase in amortization, and a $91 million earnout charge. Those amounts show that the post-Silvus perimeter is significant, but aggregate acquisition disclosure, seasonality, and nonrecurring items prevent isolation of Silvus owner earnings or a reliable net direction.
audit_findings.action: Build a trailing-twelve-month or acquisition-date pro forma OE reconciliation using 2026 interim results, separately normalizing Silvus revenue, margins, interest, amortization policy, compensation, integration costs, taxes, working capital, the earnout remeasurement, Hytera gains, and the $60 million tariff refund; then rerun every scenario from the reconciled perimeter.
